note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one City of Spokane page, the Recreational Fields and Sports page, whose "Tennis and Pickleball Courts" section lists every park with a court, a street address and a count, plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. The City's page cannot be fetched by a script, because my.spokanecity.org answers every scripted request with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial, so it was read in a browser on 7 September 2026 and saved as text. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped on the two tennis courts at A.M. Cannon Park, in the West Central neighbourhood north of the river.

The City counts this park on two lists and the counts match. Its "Tennis Courts Striped for Pickleball" list reads "A.M. Cannon Park, 1511 N. Elm St., 2 Courts", and its "Tennis Courts" list gives the same park "2 Courts". That is one pickleball court to a tennis court, where Comstock, Mission and Peaceful Valley have two. So the two pickleball courts here are the two tennis courts, shared with tennis, not lined side by side across them.

Nothing else about the park is stated: no hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets, no price.
slots.getting_there:
1511 N Elm St, Spokane, WA 99201. The City writes it "1511 N. Elm St.", and the Census address geocoder matched that as written, at house-number level, in Spokane County and the incorporated place Spokane. The park is in the West Central neighbourhood, north of the river.

The City publishes nothing about parking here, nothing about transit and nothing about where the courts sit inside the park.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts is one game at a time, and a wait if a game is on when you arrive. The pickleball courts and the tennis courts are the same two slabs, so a tennis match takes half the venue and two of them take all of it.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar for permits is published. Hours, lighting, surface and nets are all unstated, and the City never writes "outdoor" against any court on the page.

faqs.a: Two pickleball courts, striped on the park's two tennis courts. The City's striped list reads "A.M. Cannon Park, 1511 N. Elm St., 2 Courts", and its tennis list gives the same park two courts.
Not stated. The City says the courts are first-come-first-served and can be officially reserved with a reservation permit by online form; it publishes no price and never says the courts are free.

faqs.q: Are the courts lit, and what are the hours?
faqs.a: Neither is stated. The City's section carries no hours and no lighting for any park, so both read as not verified here.

slots.description:
Twelve pickleball courts striped on the six tennis courts at Comstock Park on the South Hill, the second-largest set in Spokane.

The City's two lists give the two numbers that describe this venue. "Tennis Courts Striped for Pickleball" reads "Comstock Park, 601 W. 29th Ave., 12 Courts"; "Tennis Courts" reads "Comstock Park, 601 W. 29th Ave., 6 Courts". Two pickleball courts to a tennis court, on six slabs, shared with tennis. Six is the number of courts you are sharing.

The imported dataset held Comstock at four courts and at "3012 S Howard St"; the City says twelve at 601 W 29th Ave, and Howard Street and 29th Avenue bound the same park. Nothing else about the park is stated: no hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets, no price.
slots.getting_there:
601 W 29th Ave, Spokane, WA 99203. The City writes it "601 W. 29th Ave.", and the Census address geocoder matched that as written, at house-number level, in Spokane County and the incorporated place Spokane.

The City publishes nothing about parking, nothing about transit, and nothing about where in the park the six tennis courts stand.
slots.what_to_expect:
Twelve courts if nobody is playing tennis, and two fewer for every tennis match under way, because each tennis court carries two pickleball courts. The City publishes no schedule for either sport, so how many of the twelve are yours is decided on arrival.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar is published.

Hours, lighting, surface and nets are all unstated.

faqs.a: Twelve pickleball courts, striped on six tennis courts. The City's striped list reads "Comstock Park, 601 W. 29th Ave., 12 Courts" and its tennis list "6 Courts" for the same park.

faqs.q: Why did the count change from four to twelve?
faqs.a: The imported dataset held four courts at 3012 S Howard St. The City's own list says twelve at 601 W 29th Ave, and the operator's stated count is the one that publishes. The change is flagged for re-check.
Not stated. The imported dataset said "Free public play"; the City writes no price and never says the courts are free, so that note was removed and cost reads as unstated.

slots.description:
Sixteen pickleball courts striped on the eight tennis courts at Mission Park in the Logan neighbourhood, the largest set in Spokane.

The City's striped list reads "Mission Park, 1208 E. Mission Ave., 16 Courts" and its tennis list "Mission Park, 1208 E. Mission Ave., 8 Courts": two pickleball courts to a tennis court, on eight slabs, shared with tennis. Sixteen is a stripe count, the number of pickleball courts that exist when no tennis is being played on any of the eight. It is also the largest court count at any verified venue in Washington.

No hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets and no price are stated for the park.
slots.getting_there:
1208 E Mission Ave, Spokane, WA 99202. The City writes it "1208 E. Mission Ave.", and the Census address geocoder matched that as written, at house-number level, in Spokane County and the incorporated place Spokane. The park is in the Logan neighbourhood and shares its postcode with Underhill Park to the south-east.

The City publishes nothing about parking, nothing about transit, and nothing about where in the park the eight tennis courts stand.
slots.what_to_expect:
Sixteen courts at most, and two fewer for every tennis match in progress. With eight tennis courts this is the park where the City's own description of its tennis courts, which "host neighborhood pick-up games, parks and recreation classes and many tennis events", has the most room to apply. A tennis event on eight courts is sixteen pickleball courts you cannot use.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar is published, so a reserved court is not something you can check before you leave.

Hours, lighting, surface and nets are all unstated.

faqs.a: Sixteen pickleball courts, striped on eight tennis courts, the largest set in Spokane. The City's striped list reads "Mission Park, 1208 E. Mission Ave., 16 Courts".

faqs.q: Are the courts shared with tennis?
faqs.a: Yes. The City's tennis list gives the park eight tennis courts, and its striped list sixteen pickleball courts; each tennis court carries two.
Not stated. The City publishes no price and never says the courts are free; the imported dataset's "Free public play" note was removed because the operator does not say it.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped on the one tennis court at Peaceful Valley Park, below the bluff west of downtown.

The City's striped list reads "Peaceful Valley Park, 1602 W. Water Ave., 2 Courts" and its tennis list "Peaceful Valley Park, 1602 W. Water Ave., 1 Court". Two pickleball courts on a single tennis court, the same two-to-one arrangement as Comstock and Mission at the smallest scale the City lists. Both courts share the one slab, so the venue is either pickleball or tennis at any moment and not both.

No hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets and no price are stated.

Water Ave.", and the Census address geocoder matched that as written, at house-number level, in Spokane County and the incorporated place Spokane. It shares a postcode with A.M. Cannon Park. If an older listing gives the park on North Maple Street, the City's house number is the one published here.

The City publishes nothing about parking, nothing about transit and nothing about where in the park the court is.
slots.what_to_expect:
One slab, two pickleball courts on it, and whichever sport arrived first. Two courts is a game rather than a rotation, and here a single tennis match takes both of them.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar is published, so this page cannot tell you whether the court is reserved on a given evening.

Hours, lighting, surface and nets are all unstated.

faqs.a: Two pickleball courts, striped on the park's one tennis court. The City's striped list reads "Peaceful Valley Park, 1602 W. Water Ave., 2 Courts" and its tennis list "1 Court".

faqs.q: Why does the address differ from older listings?
faqs.a: The imported dataset held a street range, "100-198 N Maple St", which does not resolve to a house number. The City publishes 1602 W Water Ave, which does, and that is what is here.
Not stated. The City publishes no price and never says the courts are free. The dataset's "Free public play" note was removed for that reason.

slots.description:
Two dedicated pickleball courts at Corbin Park, the oval park in the Emerson-Garfield neighbourhood north of downtown.

This park is on two of the City's lists for two different sports. Its "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" list reads "Corbin Park, 2914 N. West Oval St, 2 Courts", courts built for pickleball rather than lines on a tennis court, and its "Tennis Courts" list reads "Corbin Park, 2914 N. West Oval St, 1 Court". Unlike the four striped venues in Spokane, a tennis match at Corbin does not take a pickleball court away.

No hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets and no price are stated for the park.

The City publishes nothing about parking, nothing about transit and nothing about where on the oval the courts are.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts that are pickleball courts whenever you arrive; the City's word is "Dedicated". Two courts is one game at a time and a wait if both are taken.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar is published, so a court under permit is something you find out about at the fence.

Hours, lighting and surface are unstated, and nets are not mentioned for any court on the page, so whether a dedicated court here has a permanent net is not on the record.

faqs.a: Two dedicated pickleball courts. The City's "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" list reads "Corbin Park, 2914 N. West Oval St, 2 Courts".
No. The City lists one tennis court at Corbin Park on its tennis list; it is a tennis court, and the two pickleball courts are on a separate list.
Not stated. The City publishes no price and never says the courts are free; the imported dataset's "Public" note is not a price either.

slots.description:
Two dedicated pickleball courts at Underhill Park in the East Central neighbourhood.

The City's "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" list reads "Underhill Park, 2910 E. Hartson Ave., 2 Courts", courts built for pickleball rather than lines on a tennis court. The park is on no other list in the section: it does not appear under "Tennis Courts" at all, which makes it the one pickleball venue in Spokane with no tennis court beside it. At the four striped parks a tennis match takes pickleball courts away; here there is nothing to share with.

No hours, no lighting, no surface, no nets and no price are stated for the park.

slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts that are pickleball courts whenever you arrive, and no tennis at the park to compete for them. Two courts is one game at a time, so the only thing between you and a court is whoever got there first.

The City states that the courts are "first-come-first-served", and that a court can be officially reserved with "a reservation permit" by online form. No price, lead time or calendar is published.

Hours, lighting and surface are unstated, and nets are not mentioned for any court on the page. What the record does say plainly is the count and the kind: two courts, dedicated, at an address that resolves.

Not on the City's list. Underhill Park is on the dedicated pickleball list and not on the tennis list, so the pickleball courts share the park with no tennis.
